tiktok.author: helpmeexitvi
tiktok.body:
thoughts on GH’s availability blog post and their recent spat of incidents + merge queue regression update! #github #reliabilityengineering #Tech
Last week the CTO of Github published this update on Github availability. This write up came out five days after the merge queue regression, which I guess was caused by a code path that was supposed to be gated by a feature flag, but the gating was incomplete and as a result, PRS that were merged and merge queue had a chance that they weren't rebased correctly and old code was getting deployed. And this article came out one day after Github announced that Co Pilot is moving to usage based billing. Is attributing the availability issues in Github with the acceleration of agentic coding. There are a couple paragraphs about what they've done recently, including their migration to Azure. CTO of Github claimed that this migration to Azure at the time was like necessary for hyperscale, for running co pilot and having enough GPU and compute. I mean, wasn't necessary maybe. Was it because they were acquired by Microsoft? Yes. They go through some other work that they've done, like isolating critical services to minimize blast radius. All of this is fine, but I think two things are really disappointing about this response. One is that, like, it doesn't really feel satisfactory. Like, it's like, I understand that there's this hyperscale issue and AI and slop coding at velocity, but I also think that gethub owes us more of an explanation than, you know, testing didn't find it or validation didn't find it because the regression wasn't a bug. It was the core function of how merge queues work. They do say they're gonna work to increase transparency, but I do find their summaries a little lacking, uh, both because of the role that get up plays in so many ecosystems, and also because of their trying to up pricing in so many ways recently. For instance, this is a screenshot from the incident report after the big AWS US East 1 outage with Dynamodb. That has, like, way more detail than just we didn't fully gate a feature flag, which is the point of a retrospective. But, uh, clearly there is a problem, and I don't think it's outlandish to say there are a lot of conversations going on right now about how to decouple from gethub because of it.
